The catalogue includes technology stocks, cryptocurrencies, currencies, commodities and ETFs. Comparing them can illustrate different position values and asset descriptions. A category label does not measure suitability, safety, expected returns or current momentum.

TradeHQ's $100,000 virtual portfolio lets you compare hypothetical positions across these categories without using real money. Record the assumptions behind a practice decision and review what the simulator can and cannot reproduce.

Step 1 of 5 · Understand
A quote is not a guaranteed execution price.

Imagine buying two shares of a fictional company, Northstar, at a displayed price of $50 each. The quoted trade value would be $100. If the simulator charges a 0.1% fee, the estimated total cost is $100.10. In real markets, a market order may execute at a different price from the last quote.

2 shares × $50 = $100.00 before fees

$100 × 0.001 = $0.10 simulated fee

Estimated cash used = $100.10

Which statement is accurate?

The last displayed quote guarantees the final execution price.The execution price can differ; fees also change the cash used.Buying a share guarantees a positive return.

title: About TradeHQ | Educational Paper Trading Simulator
mainText:
About TradeHQ

TradeHQ exists to make financial education more accessible through practical learning. It is an educational simulator — not a brokerage, not an advisor.

Mission

Make financial literacy practical. TradeHQ lets learners place simulated market buys and sells, observe how orders and labelled practice prices affect portfolio value, and study the outcomes using virtual money.

Vision

A world where the first exposure to trading is educational, not expensive. Beginners should be able to make — and learn from — their first thousand mistakes on a simulator, not on their savings.

Educational Philosophy

Worked examples and virtual exercises complement reading. Every feature — the $100,000 virtual portfolio, the educational mentor, the daily challenge, the wiki and the compound growth simulator — exists to turn abstract concepts (risk, position sizing, diversification, psychology) into things you can feel through hands-on practice.

Open the hypothetical compound growth calculator

Transparency

TradeHQ is not a brokerage. We do not custody funds, execute real trades, or provide financial advice. Prices shown are simulated or delayed and are for education only. Third-party advertising and optional analytics are described in the privacy policy; their operation depends on provider settings and applicable user choices.

Technology

TradeHQ is a modern web application built with React, TypeScript and a serverless backend. Guest practice records stay in your browser so you can start without signing up. Account cash, positions and server-recorded trades restore across devices when available; earlier guest trade history and journals remain browser-held; signed-in lessons and beginner-journey progress can sync privately when online. The standalone mentor uses a built-in answer library and local topic matching without an AI API request; portfolio mentor tools can use simulated portfolio context.

Creator

TradeHQ was created by Anuga Weerasinghe as an educational software project focused on helping beginners understand financial markets through simulation and structured learning.

What TradeHQ Is Not
Not a brokerage — no real orders are ever routed to any exchange.
Not a financial or investment advisor — nothing on the site is a recommendation to buy or sell.
Not a source of live, guaranteed market data — prices are simulated or delayed for education.
Not a substitute for professional advice — talk to a licensed advisor before investing real money.
How the material is written and reviewed

TradeHQ uses AI-assisted drafting and editing for educational material and software. Checks include worked-example arithmetic, consistency with simulator features and source suitability within the scope recorded on each page. These checks do not establish that every statement is correct or independently reviewed by a professional. References may provide background rather than evidence that a strategy predicts prices. Options and futures lessons are conceptual; the simulator does not execute those contracts.

Community Reviews publish visitor-submitted feedback; we do not independently verify reviewers' identities or experiences. The Community Practice Board publishes optional, server-recorded ranked simulated portfolios, with earlier browser-reported results labelled separately. These are not independently verified investment results. Neither feedback nor practice rankings promise real-world returns. Educational figures use cited sources or clearly labelled hypothetical examples; when a question has no honest answer — which asset will rise, whether a strategy will work for you — the page says so instead of guessing. Content is revised whenever a reader points out an error or a market mechanism changes, and corrections are made in place rather than quietly removed.

What to expect when you write to us

TradeHQ is a small independent project rather than a company with a support desk, so messages are read and answered by the person who builds the site. In practice that means response times vary with request volume and can take longer over a weekend or a public holiday. Nothing is auto-responded to by TradeHQ. You can open an email draft or copy it into webmail. Where configured, a separate direct-send option delivers a validated message through Cloudflare and an email provider to the maintainer; the app does not retain it in its own database.

Bug reports are the most useful thing you can send. If something behaved unexpectedly, include the page address you were on, the browser and device you were using, what you expected to happen and what actually happened. A screenshot removes most of the guesswork. For a problem with a simulated trade, mention the ticker and roughly when it happened. Guest positions are browser-held; signed-in cash and open positions may also be stored by account sync when that service is available. Do not send passwords or private financial records.

Feature suggestions are welcome and genuinely do shape the public roadmap — several of the items already shipped started as a message from a reader. If you are writing about a partnership, an educational collaboration or use of the material in a classroom, say so in the subject line and include enough detail that the first reply can be a useful one rather than a request for more information.

What we cannot help with

We cannot tell you what to buy or sell, review your real portfolio, or comment on whether a particular asset is a good investment. TradeHQ is an educational simulator and is not a broker, an adviser or a research house, so any such answer would be both unhelpful and inappropriate. Questions about tax, residency rules or the legality of a real brokerage account in your country need a licensed professional where you live — the country guides point to the relevant regulator, but they are context, not advice.

Guest practice records are stored in the browser that created them. Optional account sync stores account cash, positions and server-recorded trades for restoration on another device when the service is available. Earlier guest trade history and journal entries remain browser-held. Guest lesson progress and badges are saved in the browser; signed-in lesson completion, unfinished quiz answers, reading position and first-trade journey progress can also be synced privately between devices when online. Clearing browser data removes the local copy, but does not delete a saved account record. Daily streaks and private journals are not included in the learning sync, and portfolio backups do not restore lessons.

mainText:
Privacy Policy

This policy describes the data flows used by the current TradeHQ website, including optional analytics and advertising.

Last Updated: November 22, 2026

Privacy at a Glance
✓
Core simulator features can be used without creating an account.
✓
Guest portfolios stay in your browser; account cash, positions and server-recorded trades restore from Supabase.
✓
Optional accounts and community features can store data with Supabase.
✓
Optional Arena and leaderboard-to-registration analytics require fresh adult opt-in; session replay and automatic interaction capture are disabled. Google advertising has separate privacy choices.
✓
Cloudflare performance measurement and Google Fonts requests are separate from the optional Amplitude choice and can run before a choice or after rejection.
✓
No real-money deposit or brokerage account is required for simulated trading.
Information TradeHQ Handles
TradeHQ can be used without creating an account. The data handled depends on the features you choose.

• Guest simulator data: practice cash, positions and trade history are stored in your browser with a separate browser-local recovery copy. You can download or explicitly restore a portable practice backup JSON file containing trading history and any private journal notes. The backup feature does not upload this file. Backup formats can be manually edited: TradeHQ validates file structure and arithmetic but does not certify authenticity, investment performance or leaderboard ranking. An imported guest file remains unverified. Guest learning-journey progress, course progress, streaks and related settings remain browser-stored. For signed-in users, lesson completion, unfinished quiz answers, reading position and first-trade journey progress may also be saved privately in Supabase and synchronized across devices when online. New beginner-journey reflection text stays on the device. Older reflections already synchronized remain private in the account. Streaks and unrelated browser preferences are not part of this account sync.
• Signed-in portfolio data: Supabase stores account cash, positions and server-recorded practice orders, including asset, quantity, execution price, fees, time and simulated result. These account records restore across devices when the service is available. Signed-in users can also download a server-signed current-cycle historical practice export and verify its integrity against their authenticated account. This file may contain account identifiers and private transaction details; it is not publicly shared or accepted as an upload that replaces ranked trades. A first-time browser import stores cash and positions as an unranked portfolio; earlier guest trade history stays in its original browser. Starting a fresh ranked practice cycle archives the previous account snapshot privately. Journals remain browser-held; signed-in lesson and beginner-journey progress can sync privately and are not used to determine public trading ranks.
• Optional account data: if you create an account, Supabase processes authentication data such as your email or provider identity and can store profile fields including username, country and bio.
• Foundations assessments and certificates: when a signed-in learner uses the optional Foundations programme, Supabase stores account-linked assessment identifiers, scores, possible points and qualifying learning dates. When a learner requests a certificate, TradeHQ stores the recipient name they provide, the programme and milestone, template version, issue date and qualifying assessment evidence so the same certificate can be retrieved. Name corrections are retained as revision history; an earlier name is not erased simply by correcting it. Optional verification sharing stores a hash of the verification credential and its name revision. A person given a valid verification link can check the programme version, milestone and issue date, not the recipient name or private scores. The learner can withdraw or replace the verification link; correcting the name invalidates the previous link. Account deletion cascades to these account-linked Foundations records. A downloaded PDF or copy shared outside TradeHQ is not removed by withdrawing verification or deleting an account.
• Community data: signed-in features can store selected practice statistics, public-profile settings, reviews and duel/challenge records. A separate setting, OFF by default, lets a member voluntarily disclose up to 20 current-cycle server-recorded simulated trade entries on an otherwise public profile: asset, buy/sell, quantity, execution price, fee and date. The public data response also includes trade total, simulated realised profit/loss where recorded, and price-source information, even when a visible profile row shows fewer fields. Private journals, reflections, past cycles and browser-only records are never shared by this feature. These are simulated results, not brokerage statements or verified real-money performance. Creating or joining a practice duel requires public profiles. Eligible public duel responses include participant identifiers, invite code, recorded starting values, score values and relevant dates; other visitors may read them while the applicable profiles are public. Switching a profile to private restricts new non-participant access under the duel access policy; participants can retain access, and previously viewed copies cannot be recalled.
• Review submissions and interactions: TradeHQ stores your submitted display name (if provided), review text, rating, moderation status and an IP-derived hash used for duplicate prevention. The hash is restricted to authorized backend processing; it is not a public review field. A hash is not necessarily anonymous information. Likes are stored with your account ID and the review ID to enforce one like per account. Public pages show totals, not individual liker identities. Owner replies are public. Reviews removed from public view remain in the private admin panel for restoration. Contact TradeHQ for privacy or removal requests.
• Optional TradeHQ Newsletter: if you explicitly request the educational newsletter, TradeHQ stores your email address, consent/confirmation status, the date and source of signup, unsubscribe status, and delivery receipts in private Supabase records. Resend handles email delivery and receives your address for confirmations and issues. We never add prior contact records to the mailing list without permission. Every newsletter provides an unsubscribe link, and you may use the contact page to request deletion.
• Contact messages: by default the contact page opens your email app or lets you copy a draft into webmail. If the optional direct-send service is configured, Cloudflare Turnstile processes challenge and connection information and Resend processes the message, sender reply address and recipient information to deliver it to the maintainer's inbox. TradeHQ does not retain direct-send message bodies in its application database. The maintainer's email provider retains delivered messages according to its settings.
• Technical data: hosting, authentication, security and abuse-prevention services can receive normal request information such as IP address, browser/device information and server logs.
• Website performance: current pages load Cloudflare Web Analytics to measure page loading and performance. Its browser beacon can send the page URL, a page-load identifier, timing and browser performance measurements to Cloudflare, separately from optional Amplitude events. These performance requests can run before an analytics choice and after Amplitude is rejected. Cloudflare states that its Web Analytics usage metrics do not use cookies, local storage or fingerprinting to track individuals. This does not mean that network requests contain no connection information or that every jurisdiction exempts this processing from privacy requirements.
• Font delivery: pages request stylesheets and font files from Google Fonts. Google receives the connecting IP address, the requested resource URL and request headers, which can include browser/operating-system information and the referring page according to browser settings. These requests are separate from Amplitude consent and may occur before a choice or after rejection. Google states that its Fonts API does not set or log cookies and does not use Fonts information to create end-user profiles or for targeted advertising.
• Optional analytics and advertising data: TradeHQ offers a newly scoped analytics choice only to visitors affirmatively confirming they are at least 18. This confirmation is for optional analytics; it is not an age restriction on lessons, guest practice or sign-in. Visitors under 18 should reject optional analytics. If accepted, Amplitude can receive limited Practice Arena milestone events and two leaderboard registration-flow events (an eligible signed-out leaderboard visit, and a newly created account subsequently authenticated in that same browser within seven days), along with its pseudonymous browser identity and ordinary network metadata. The two leaderboard custom events contain no email, account ID, username, profile details, portfolio data, transaction information, or form content. The temporary seven-day same-browser attribution marker stores only a visit timestamp and is cleared on consent rejection or successful attribution. No custom Amplitude events are sent when optional analytics is declined; the website does not claim visitor identity is anonymous. Amplitude's automatic page, click, form, network and attribution collection and session replay are disabled; the two explicitly triggered attribution events are the only leaderboard funnel measurement. Earlier v1/v2 analytics permissions are not reused. Google AdSense has separate advertising choices and may use cookies or similar identifiers for ad delivery, measurement and, where applicable, personalisation.
• Practice Arena research: exercise decisions, private written reasons, closing reflections and history stay in your browser and are not automatically submitted to a research database. An optional, adult-only research questionnaire keeps answers on the open page and only prepares an email if you deliberately choose to do so; you must send that email yourself. Sending an email reveals your sender address and may include other email-provider metadata. Answers are not anonymous once linked with a sender or identifying comments. If you accept Amplitude analytics, TradeHQ may record Arena view/start/finish/resume milestones, scenario ID and difficulty, and whether this browser returned on a later day. Custom Arena events do not include trading choices, portfolio values, account IDs, written notes or questionnaire answers. This opt-in measurement uses the existing Amplitude service's consented visitor identity; it does not create a separate TradeHQ research identifier. Declining analytics disables those custom milestones. A same-browser return event does not prove a person learned or voluntarily returned.

TradeHQ does not require a payment card, bank account or brokerage account to place simulated trades.
How Information Is Used
TradeHQ uses data only for the feature that needs it: operating the simulator, authenticating optional accounts, showing profile/community features, preventing abuse, responding to messages, delivering a voluntarily confirmed TradeHQ Newsletter subscription, diagnosing problems and improving the service.

Amplitude is used for limited, explicitly triggered Arena and leaderboard-to-new-account registration analytics after renewed adult opt-in. TradeHQ measures only consenting eligible visitors and same-browser new-account confirmations within seven days; email-link confirmations in another browser and visitors who reject analytics are not included, so any conversion rate is an incomplete proxy, not a claim about all visitors. This site's Amplitude configuration disables session replay, automatic page and click capture, form interactions, network tracking and remote automatic-enablement settings. We do not claim that disabling those features makes Amplitude's pseudonymous identifiers or request metadata anonymous.

Ad-serving scripts and placements are currently disabled on TradeHQ, including newly published courses, account pages and error screens. The publisher verification meta tag and ads.txt do not enable ad serving. Before advertising can be enabled, TradeHQ must verify Google site approval, suitable reviewed inventory, placement controls and applicable consent configuration. If advertising is enabled, Google and its partners may place or read cookies and use similar technologies, web beacons, IP addresses and other identifiers to deliver and measure ads. Third parties may collect information as a result of ad serving. Advertising cookies can reflect prior visits to TradeHQ or other sites and, where consent and law permit, support personalised ads. These uses remain subject to the applicable privacy choices. Advertising may be personalized, non-personalized or limited depending on consent, location and Google settings.

TradeHQ does not sell simulated portfolio data to brokers or financial institutions and does not execute real-money trades.
Storage, Visibility & Retention
Browser data remains on the device until the browser, the user or TradeHQ's own reset controls remove it. Clearing all site data also removes browser-local recovery copies; download a portfolio backup to preserve it separately. Clearing browser data removes local records; it does not delete a signed-in portfolio already stored in Supabase.

Optional account and community data can be stored by Supabase for as long as the related account or feature requires it. Newsletter consent records and delivery receipts are retained while relevant to operating the requested subscription, unsubscribe suppression, and compliance; contact TradeHQ to request deletion or information. New accounts start with a private profile. You may explicitly make your profile public later; only then can chosen profile fields and selected simulated statistics appear on public pages. Existing members retain their chosen visibility, and public trade-history sharing remains a separate off-by-default permission.

Scored educational trophy challenges are optional for registered users. TradeHQ stores the minimal account-linked challenge ID, source version, pass/miss and score receipt, and the resulting permanent trophy ID and issue date. It does not store the answer choices you selected, your written Arena notes or a copy of each Daily case in the trophy award record. Existing device-only learning progress is not used to create server-verified public awards. Account deletion removes the separate trophy records.

Trophy display is disabled by default even for a public trader profile, including older profiles that were historically public by default. After an account is confirmed and its profile is deliberately public, the owner may separately enable display of one earned trophy flair and up to three earned pinned trophies. Only the chosen trophy names/icons are shown publicly; scores, assessment dates, balances, trades, contacts and private learning history are not included. You may withdraw this permission in My Trophy Cabinet, or hide the entire profile; both actions stop the optional trophy display.

The optional leaderboard attribution marker contains only a local visit timestamp and is eligible for matching for no more than seven days. If the person does not return, the expired timestamp may remain in browser storage until the next relevant page access, consent withdrawal or site-data clearing; it is then discarded or replaced. A successful attributed registration also clears the marker. Analytics and advertising data at external providers are retained according to their settings and policies; TradeHQ does not state a fixed provider retention period where it cannot verify one.

TradeHQ uses hosted infrastructure and access controls intended to protect stored data, but no online service can guarantee absolute security.
Age and Optional Features
The core simulator works without an account. The optional account flow does not ask for age, so TradeHQ does not determine a visitor's age from that form.

Public profiles and community features can publish the information and simulated statistics you choose to share. Avoid including private or sensitive information in public fields. A parent or guardian can use the contact page to raise a privacy concern involving a young user. Optional Amplitude Arena and leaderboard registration-flow analytics are unavailable unless the visitor confirms they are at least 18 and affirmatively accepts the updated permission. This declaration is not verified age assurance and does not resolve every jurisdiction's child-safety requirements. Visitors under 18 should reject analytics; the core simulator remains available.

An advertising consent choice alone does not determine age or replace age-specific advertising protections where they apply.
Service Providers, Cookies & Your Choices
TradeHQ relies on third parties including Cloudflare Pages for hosting and Cloudflare Web Analytics for page-performance measurement, Google Fonts for stylesheet and font delivery, Supabase for optional authentication/database features, Resend for explicitly requested newsletter emails and contact messages, Amplitude for optional adult-consented Arena and leaderboard-to-registration analytics without session replay, and, if advertising is enabled in a future reviewed release, Google AdSense for consented advertising. These providers can process data in countries other than your own under their own legal and contractual arrangements.

Optional Amplitude scripts are blocked unless a visitor expressly confirms they are at least 18 and accepts the newly expanded analytics choice. Prior v1 and v2 choices are not carried forward. Accepting stores a pseudonymous Amplitude browser identifier locally to support consented Arena measurement and the limited same-browser leaderboard registration funnel. You can reject analytics or withdraw a previous choice from this privacy page; withdrawal stops new custom events but does not automatically erase historical events already held by a provider. Contact TradeHQ for a privacy or deletion request. The Amplitude choice does not control the Cloudflare performance or Google Fonts requests described above. Analytics acceptance does not grant advertising consent.

Before any future advertising release, TradeHQ must verify the applicable Google-certified consent-management configuration for regional advertising choices in the EEA, United Kingdom and Switzerland. Availability of the published message depends on Google's configuration and the visitor's region; an unavailable message does not constitute consent. The Google message lets you consent, decline or manage individual options. When it applies, use Advertising privacy choices on this page or in the footer to change or withdraw your decision.

In supported US states, Google's Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information link lets you opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information for advertising. Google applies restricted data processing to applicable opt-out requests. These regional messages manage Google's advertising partners; optional Amplitude analytics are controlled separately.

You can also clear browser storage/cookies, use browser privacy controls and manage ad personalization through Google Ads Settings. When the Google message is available, its partner list describes the vendors and purposes covered by your advertising choices.

Depending on where you live, privacy law may give you rights to access, correct, delete, restrict or object to certain processing. Use the TradeHQ contact page for a privacy request. The exact rights available depend on your jurisdiction.

What is Short Squeeze?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. Limited source check: 2026-11-01. Checked short-sale closing mechanics, periodic short-interest snapshots, the days-to-cover formula and 10 × ($28 − $20) = $80 illustrative loss against FINRA sources. No individual squeeze event, predictive signal or historical return series was verified. This is not independent professional review.

A short squeeze occurs when a rising price or difficulty borrowing a security puts pressure on short sellers to close positions by buying shares. That covering demand can add further upward pressure to the price.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A short seller borrows a security, sells it, and later needs to buy equivalent securities to close the position and return what was borrowed. If the price rises instead of falling, the short position loses value. A short squeeze can develop when price increases or borrowing constraints cause multiple short sellers to cover at the same time; those purchases add demand and can intensify the upward move. Short interest is one useful measure of outstanding short positions, while days to cover compares reported short interest with average daily share volume. FINRA publishes these measures as market data, but they do not create a universal squeeze threshold or a reliable timing signal. Reported short interest is also a periodic snapshot rather than a real-time count. Borrowing availability, trading volume, price movement, liquidity and the behaviour of market participants can all affect whether heavy short positioning ever becomes a squeeze.

KEY POINTS
A squeeze can occur when rising prices or borrowing pressure cause short sellers to cover
Covering purchases can add further upward pressure to the price
Short interest and days to cover provide context but do not define a universal squeeze threshold
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Treat short interest and days-to-cover figures as context, not a trigger. Compare current reported data with earlier periods and check how the price and trading volume are behaving; no single percentage or ratio guarantees that a squeeze will occur.

Worked exercise and its limits

Hypothetical short-sale worksheet: 10 borrowed shares sold at $20 and repurchased at $28 create an $80 loss before borrowing costs. Explain why buying to cover adds demand, while a price rise alone cannot reveal who bought. TradeHQ cannot open short positions.

References and scope

FINRA — short-interest data fields and days-to-cover calculation

What is Golden Cross?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A golden cross labels a shorter moving average crossing above a longer one, often the 50-day above the 200-day. It describes historical averages and does not establish that prices will continue rising.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A golden cross labels a shorter moving average crossing above a longer one; 50-day and 200-day simple averages are a common convention. Each average summarizes selected past closing prices. The crossover can arrive after a substantial price rise, and a subsequent reversal can produce another crossover. Changing the interval, lookback or price adjustment changes the observations. The label does not reveal institutional orders or establish a profitable entry. For a comparison, state the dataset and rules before reviewing later prices, include failed examples and account for costs. A generated practice chart cannot establish how a rule performed in real historical markets.

KEY POINTS
50-day MA crossing above the 200-day MA is the classic setup
Calculated from past prices; a crossover can lag or reverse
Does not establish future buying activity or a profitable entry
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

The golden cross compares historical averages; the crossover does not establish what price will do next.

Worked exercise and its limits

On a separate historical dataset, mark a 50-period average crossing a 200-period average. Freeze the interval and settings before looking forward; include later failed crosses. TradeHQ's generated candles cannot validate the pattern against real history.

What is Death Cross?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A death cross labels a shorter moving average crossing below a longer one, often the 50-day below the 200-day. This is a lagging price calculation, not confirmation of a future decline.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A death cross labels a shorter moving average crossing below a longer one, commonly a 50-day average below a 200-day average. It describes the relationship between selected historical averages. It need not identify the beginning of a decline, and a later recovery can reverse the crossover. The slope of either average is another historical observation, not a universal measure of signal strength. Do not infer how professional managers position portfolios from this label. To evaluate an imagined rule, specify the series, frequency, execution assumptions and comparison period before inspecting outcomes. Include costs and both continuation and recovery cases.

KEY POINTS
A 50-day average crossing below a 200-day average fits the conventional definition
A description of selected historical prices, not a validated prediction of a downturn
Compare price and volume observations without assuming confirmation predicts returns
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Mark when the selected averages cross, then compare later continuations and reversals. Recognising a historical crossover does not guarantee protection from a future decline.

Worked exercise and its limits

Construct two hypothetical paths with the same downward moving-average crossover: one recovers and one continues falling. The common crossover cannot distinguish their futures. Explain the delay caused by averaging old prices.

What is Liquidation Cascade?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A liquidation cascade is feedback in which forced position reductions add price pressure that can trigger further reductions. Venue rules, collateral and liquidity affect the outcome.

DETAILED DEFINITION

In a leveraged market, falling collateral value or adverse price changes can cause positions to breach maintenance requirements. Forced reductions may add buying or selling pressure. If that pressure worsens prices for other leveraged positions, additional liquidations can follow. Such feedback can occur in either direction and does not require a universal leverage ratio or loss threshold. Actual liquidation terms depend on the instrument, collateral, mark-price method, maintenance tiers and venue procedures. A price wick alone does not measure the amount liquidated or identify its cause. TradeHQ does not provide leveraged positions or a liquidation engine; examples remain separate arithmetic exercises.

KEY POINTS
Feedback depends on leverage, collateral rules and available liquidity
Forced reductions can amplify an adverse move; totals require event-specific evidence
Candle wicks alone cannot establish whether a cascade occurred
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare a hypothetical price shock with documented margin rules. A cascade label does not establish exact liquidation levels. TradeHQ does not implement leveraged positions or margin calls.

Worked exercise and its limits

A hypothetical $1,000 collateral amount supports $10,000 exposure. A 5% adverse price change creates a $500 loss before costs. Actual liquidation depends on maintenance requirements and venue rules; TradeHQ does not simulate forced liquidation.

What is Fibonacci Retracement?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

Fibonacci retracement plots conventional fractions of a selected price swing, often 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8% and 78.6%. The 50% level is a common chart convention, not a Fibonacci ratio, and none of these lines guarantees support or resistance.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A retracement drawing selects a price high and low, then marks fractions of their difference. Common chart conventions include 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8% and 78.6%; 50% is a midpoint convention rather than a Fibonacci-sequence ratio. The chosen endpoints and interval materially change the levels. Arithmetic does not establish that buyers or sellers will appear at a marked price. Several drawings can fit the same history, so specify the endpoints before reviewing later candles and keep cases where price passes through the levels. The background reference explains historical chart analysis, not a measured success rate for these ratios.

KEY POINTS
Key levels: 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, and 78.6%
61.8% is a selected reference ratio, not a probability of a reversal
Combining chart tools does not establish a success probability
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Calculate the levels from a clearly identified high and low, then compare how changing those anchors changes the chart. A Fibonacci ratio alone does not establish a reversal probability.

Worked exercise and its limits

For an invented rise from $80 to $120, a 50% retracement is $100 and a 61.8% retracement is $95.28. These are selected arithmetic levels, not probabilities. Sketch both a rebound and a continuation through each level.

What is RSI Divergence?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. Limited source check: 2026-11-01. Checked Fidelity's RSI scale and divergence explanation and the stipulated $100/$95 and RSI 25/32 comparison. These are input values, not calculated RSI; no predictive performance, historical backtest or TradeHQ indicator equivalence was verified. This is not independent professional review.

RSI divergence describes a mismatch between selected price swings and RSI swings. It can be followed by continuation or reversal, so it is not a dependable forecast by itself.

DETAILED DEFINITION

Standard RSI compares smoothed upward and downward price changes over a selected lookback and expresses their relative strength on a 0–100 scale. A divergence compares its selected swings with price swings: for example, a lower price low alongside a higher RSI low. Those observations can occur before either a reversal or continued decline. Changing the interval or which swings count changes the comparison. No timeframe is established here as reliably predictive. Use matching external price and standard RSI data for the worksheet; the RSI-style value in TradeHQ is not a standard historical RSI calculation.

KEY POINTS
Bullish divergence: price lower low + RSI higher low
Bearish divergence: price higher high + RSI lower high
Results depend on the sample and settings; no reliable timeframe is established here
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare the price swings and RSI swings over the same dates and settings. Record both divergences followed by reversals and those followed by continuation; divergence is not an entry guarantee.

Worked exercise and its limits

Invent two observations from one matching interval: at A, price is $100 and standard RSI is 25; at B, price is $95 and RSI is 32. Price makes a lower low while RSI makes a higher low, so these stipulated swings show bullish divergence. The RSI values are given inputs, not values calculated from just these two prices. Extend the price path once to $105 and separately to $85: the same divergence can precede either outcome. TradeHQ’s RSI-style display is not a standard historical RSI series.

What is MACD Histogram?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

The MACD histogram represents the difference between the MACD line and signal line as vertical bars. It is calculated from past prices.

DETAILED DEFINITION

The MACD histogram is MACD minus its signal line. Under common defaults, MACD is a 12-period exponential average minus a 26-period average; the signal is a 9-period exponential average of MACD. A positive histogram means MACD exceeds the signal. Bars becoming less negative mean that difference is narrowing, not that the asset must rise. The histogram can change because either component changes. Interval, initialization and price data affect the calculation. TradeHQ does not display a MACD overlay, so calculate this example separately rather than treating the practice chart as indicator evidence.

KEY POINTS
Measures the gap between MACD line and signal line
Bars show MACD minus its signal line; a larger difference does not by itself measure price acceleration
Histogram divergence describes historical observations, not a reversal forecast
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Reproduce the difference between a MACD line and its signal line before interpreting the bars. This describes calculated observations, not a reliable entry or exit time.

Worked exercise and its limits

Hypothetical MACD = 2.0 and signal = 1.5 give a histogram of 0.5. If MACD stays 2.0 and the signal rises to 1.8, the histogram shrinks to 0.2 without MACD becoming negative. TradeHQ has no MACD overlay.

What is Bollinger Band Squeeze?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A Bollinger Band squeeze describes a narrow distance between the bands relative to a selected comparison period. It reflects lower measured volatility, without specifying the direction or size of the next move.

DETAILED DEFINITION

Bollinger Bands place upper and lower bands around a moving average using a selected measure of price dispersion. A commonly used setup is a 20-period simple average with bands two standard deviations away, but settings vary. A squeeze describes relatively narrow bands compared with a stated lookback. It does not establish when volatility will increase, which direction price will move or how far. Past price distributions need not be normal, and the bands are not a guaranteed probability interval. Record the calculation and comparison period before evaluating later candles; avoid choosing a squeeze only after seeing a large move.

KEY POINTS
Narrow bands describe lower recent volatility; they do not establish when a breakout will occur
A break outside a band is an observation that can continue or reverse
Volume provides another observation, without validating a future move
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare the bandwidth over a stated sample. Narrow bands describe recent price dispersion, without storing physical energy or identifying the next move’s size or direction.

Worked exercise and its limits

Compare band widths calculated over the same interval and settings on a separate dataset. Label the narrow period before inspecting what followed. Draw both upward and downward outcomes; narrow bands do not supply a direction or deadline.

What is Order Block?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

An order block is a chart-defined zone used in some technical-analysis frameworks; candles alone do not establish actual institutional orders. Some frameworks use the last opposing candle before a selected directional move; definitions vary.

DETAILED DEFINITION

An order block is a chart-zone label used in some trading frameworks, often for the last opposing candle before a selected directional move. Definitions differ between authors. Candles aggregate transactions and do not identify a particular institution, an unfilled order or a hidden inventory position. Terms such as mitigation and accumulation remain interpretations unless separately supported by order or participant evidence. A useful worksheet fixes the zone criteria in advance, records every revisit and includes failures. The order-mechanics reference explains actual order instructions; it does not validate an order-block forecasting method.

KEY POINTS
Interprets price zones without proving institutional accumulation or distribution
Some frameworks label the last opposing candle before a selected rise; the label does not establish actual orders
Price may revisit or move away from a marked block; continuation is uncertain
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Label the candle zone and the rule used to select it. Price candles alone cannot identify a particular institution's orders, remaining inventory or future buying intentions.

Worked exercise and its limits

Label the candle and zone criteria before viewing later candles. Record every revisit and every failure under that definition. A chart zone cannot establish an institution's actual orders; the term has no single exchange-standard definition.

What is Fair Value Gap (FVG)?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A Fair Value Gap is a three-candle chart pattern where the full price ranges of the first and third candles do not overlap. The range need not be revisited and does not establish economic fair value or unfilled orders.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A Fair Value Gap (FVG) is a three-candle chart label used in Smart Money Concepts (SMC) and Inner Circle Trader (ICT) frameworks. For an upward example, candle one’s high is below candle three’s low; for a downward example, candle one’s low is above candle three’s high. The marked range depends on the selected candles, interval and data source. It does not establish economic fair value, a market-efficiency violation, unfilled orders or the identity and intentions of participants. To study it, freeze the selection rules before inspecting later prices and record both revisited and unvisited ranges. Neither a longer candle interval, accompanying volume nor overlapping chart labels establishes a measured chance of a revisit or a profitable entry. Use the invented worksheet below to compare two possible later paths without treating either as a forecast.

KEY POINTS
A selected three-candle sequence with non-overlapping first and third price ranges
Labels a non-overlapping candle range that need not be revisited
Not a validated entry rule or guarantee that a gap will fill
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Identify the three candles and the non-overlapping price range. Compare examples where price revisits the range with examples where it does not; a gap need not fill or act as support.

Worked exercise and its limits

Invent three candles where the first high is $100 and the third low is $102. Mark the $100–$102 non-overlap. Then draw a path that revisits it and one that never does. Neither proves unfilled orders or economic fair value.

What is Bull Trap?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A retrospective label for a move above selected resistance followed by a downward reversal. The pattern alone does not establish buyers’ losses or anyone’s intent.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A bull trap is a retrospective label for a price move above a selected resistance area that subsequently reverses below it. The apparent breakout can encourage purchases, but a chart alone cannot establish buyers’ motives or a deliberate attempt to trap them. Definitions of resistance, breakout and reversal depend on the interval and tolerance used. At the moment of the initial break, the subsequent reversal is unknown. A study should define its criteria before looking ahead, include successful continuations as well as reversals and compare realistic fills and costs. No pattern label guarantees that an intended stop can execute at its trigger price.

KEY POINTS
A move above selected resistance followed by a reversal within the defined observation window
Define the resistance area and reversal window before counting examples or claiming a frequency
A later close below a chosen level can satisfy a stated retrospective rule; definitions vary
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Record both a breakout and its later reversal using fixed definitions. A confirmation filter changes the rule being tested; it cannot remove every failed signal.

Worked exercise and its limits

Mark a hypothetical prior high at $50, a move to $52 and a later return to $49. The label describes the later reversal; it was not known at $52. Compare losses with alternative fills and fees rather than assuming a perfect exit.

What is Whale Manipulation?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

Whale manipulation is an informal label for alleged manipulation by a large market participant. Large holdings, transfers or ordinary orders alone do not establish wrongdoing; claims about deceptive trading require evidence and the applicable market rules.

DETAILED DEFINITION

Whale is informal language for a participant or wallet with a large position. Holding or moving a large amount does not by itself establish manipulation. Spoofing involves deceptive orders intended to be cancelled rather than executed; wash-trading allegations concern transactions creating a false appearance of activity. Proving either requires evidence beyond a candlestick, displayed order or wallet transfer and depends on applicable rules. A transfer may reflect custody reorganization or another purpose unrelated to a market sale. Distinguish observable size and timing from claims about ownership, intent and price effects. Do not present alleged misconduct as a validated trading signal.

KEY POINTS
Large ownership alone does not prove spoofing, wash trading or other misconduct
Allegations require evidence and applicable market rules
On-chain analytics can track whale wallet movements in crypto
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Separate an observed transfer or order-book change from a claim about motive. Unusual size alone does not prove manipulation or identify a profitable response.

Worked exercise and its limits

Separate three observations: a large wallet transfer, a displayed order and an executed trade. List what each fails to establish about ownership, intent and economic exposure. Size alone is not evidence of unlawful activity.

What is Support and Resistance?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

Support and resistance are price areas where traders look for repeated buying or selling responses. Past reactions help define the areas but do not prevent a later price from passing through them.

DETAILED DEFINITION

Support and resistance describe price areas selected from earlier reactions or other chart rules. A past low can be used to mark support and a past high resistance, but subsequent transactions can occur beyond either. A level’s appearance depends on data frequency, adjustment, chosen tolerance and how many observations are counted. A level marked on a daily chart is not automatically more predictive than one on a shorter interval. Specify the rule before inspecting later prices, record breaks and state whether a purported reaction is an intraday observation or a close. The drawing is a description, not evidence of hidden demand or a guaranteed exit.

KEY POINTS
Support and resistance label areas of prior reactions rather than floors or ceilings
Some chart frameworks relabel a crossed level; the next reaction remains uncertain
Record the selected touches, interval and volume without ranking a level as reliably strongest
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Draw zones from specified price observations and compare alternative anchors. These are chart descriptions rather than floors, ceilings or a required first trading method.

Worked exercise and its limits

State how close prices must be to count as a touch, then mark a zone using only earlier candles. Keep later breaks in the record. Changing the zone after seeing an outcome makes the exercise vulnerable to hindsight bias.

What is Candlestick Patterns?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

Candlestick patterns are names for formations built from opening, high, low and closing prices. Traders use them to describe price action; a formation alone does not establish a reliable reversal or continuation.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A candlestick summarizes opening, high, low and closing prices for a stated interval. Its body runs between open and close; wicks extend to high and low. A doji describes a small open-to-close difference under a chosen tolerance. Engulfing patterns compare at least two candles, while names such as morning star describe longer sequences. A candle does not disclose the order of every transaction within the interval or the identity and motives of participants. Pattern definitions and data quality matter. Comparing failed and successful examples is more informative than selecting a recognizable shape only after its later outcome is known.

KEY POINTS
Single-candle examples include doji, hammer and shooting star; engulfing needs two candles
Multi-candle: morning star, evening star, three white soldiers
Context changes a pattern description but does not establish its success rate
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Read the open, high, low and close as observations. A candle shape does not reveal participant motives or the next price movement.

Worked exercise and its limits

For an invented candle with open $100, high $106, low $98 and close $104, identify body and wicks. An engulfing pattern needs at least two candles. OHLC values do not reveal the exact sequence of every trade within the interval.

CHART PATTERNS
What is Head and Shoulders?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A head and shoulders pattern has three peaks, with a higher central peak and two lower shoulders. A neckline connects the intervening lows; breaking it is a chart observation, not a confirmed future decline or guaranteed target.

DETAILED DEFINITION

The head and shoulders pattern is a commonly described reversal formation in technical analysis. It consists of three distinct peaks: a left shoulder, a higher central peak (the head), and a right shoulder that is approximately equal in height to the left shoulder. The troughs between these peaks are connected by a line called the neckline, and a break below this neckline completes the conventional pattern description; continued decline is a hypothesis that can fail. The conventional description follows five price phases; these observations do not establish participant motives. Phase one: the market trends upward and creates the left shoulder, a normal swing high. Phase two: a pullback creates the first neckline touch. Phase three: renewed buying pushes price to a higher high (the head), recording a higher observed peak, without establishing acceleration or future direction. Phase four: another pullback returns to the neckline area, and bulls attempt one more push higher. Phase five: the rally fails to reach the head's height, forming the right shoulder — a lower peak that some analysts interpret as weakening upward momentum. The measured move technique provides a price target: measure the vertical distance from the head to the neckline, then subtract that distance from the neckline breakout point. Volume adds a separate historical observation; it does not validate a forecast. Some descriptions compare volume across the shoulders, head and neckline break. State the observation window and volume source; a lower volume does not by itself establish participants’ conviction or predict the next move. Volume alone does not establish the probability that a neckline break will persist. The inverse pattern uses three troughs rather than peaks and is commonly interpreted as a bullish hypothesis, which can fail.

KEY POINTS
Three peaks: left shoulder, head (highest), right shoulder
A neckline break describes the chart; a measured target is a projection, not a guaranteed outcome
The inverse shape can occur without a lasting upward reversal
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Draw the three peaks and neckline, then distinguish the pattern's measured-move convention from the actual later price. A projected target is a hypothesis rather than an expected payout.

Worked exercise and its limits

Mark three hypothetical peaks at $50, $55 and $51 with intervening lows near $46. If you project the $9 head-to-neckline height below $46, the arithmetic target is $37. It is a projection that price need not reach.

What is Double Bottom?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A double bottom is a W-shaped chart pattern with two troughs near a similar level. A later move above the intervening peak fits the pattern, but does not ensure that a rally continues.

DETAILED DEFINITION

The double bottom is a bullish reversal pattern that forms after a sustained downtrend, characterized by two consecutive troughs at approximately the same price level separated by a moderate peak (the neckline). The pattern resembles the letter 'W' on a chart and is commonly interpreted as a possible reversal near a repeated price low; the chart alone cannot establish that selling pressure has been exhausted. The conventional description records a sequence of price observations. The first bottom forms as the existing downtrend reaches a point where buyers emerge, creating a bounce. The subsequent rally creates the neckline — the intermediate peak between the two bottoms. However, the rally loses momentum and price declines again to retest the support level established by the first bottom. The second bottom is the critical test: if price rises again from the low, it records another bounce at that level without proving the cause or durability. In the conventional chart description, a later move above the intervening peak completes the pattern; it does not confirm a lasting reversal. The measured move target equals the depth of the pattern — the distance from the bottoms to the neckline — projected upward from the neckline breakout point. Volume characteristics provide context but do not establish predictive reliability. Some descriptions compare volume during the two declines and the neckline break. Lower reported volume is an observation, not proof of reduced selling conviction or a future rebound. A volume observation does not establish a measured breakout failure rate. RSI divergence is another description of the selected historical data, not evidence of a dramatically higher success rate. If the RSI makes a higher low while price makes an equal or lower low at the second bottom, the oscillator records a smaller decline in its selected inputs; this does not validate a subsequent reversal.

KEY POINTS
W-shaped pattern with two tests of the same support level
A later move above the middle peak completes the conventional description, not a confirmed forecast
RSI divergence is another historical observation, not independent proof of a profitable reversal
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Identify the two lows and the intervening high under fixed rules, including failed examples. A familiar pattern does not establish a beginner’s readiness or confidence level.

Worked exercise and its limits

Draw troughs near $30 separated by a $35 high. The $5 height gives a conventional projection of $40 after a break above $35, but the next move could reverse. State the tolerance used to call the troughs similar.

What is Moving Average Convergence Divergence?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

MACD compares exponential moving averages of past prices. Its line, signal line and histogram describe changes in those calculations; crossovers are not reliable reversal predictions by themselves.

DETAILED DEFINITION

MACD compares exponential moving averages. With common defaults, the MACD line equals the 12-period EMA minus the 26-period EMA, the signal is a 9-period EMA of MACD and the histogram is their difference. A crossover or zero-line crossing is an event in related calculations based on past prices. It need not precede a lasting move and can repeat in a trading range. Prices, interval, initialization and settings must be stated before comparing results. The Fidelity reference documents the default calculation. TradeHQ has no MACD overlay and cannot validate a MACD rule using its generated practice candles.

KEY POINTS
MACD line = 12 EMA minus 26 EMA; Signal line = 9 EMA of MACD
Crossovers are indicator events, rather than validated buy or sell instructions
A zero-line crossing describes the relationship of the selected moving averages
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Calculate each MACD component from stated data and settings. The resulting crossings describe related averages and do not guarantee a reversal.

Worked exercise and its limits

Hypothetical 12-period EMA = $105 and 26-period EMA = $102 give MACD = $3. With a $2 signal, the histogram is $1. The values have price units; they are not percentages. Calculate separately because TradeHQ has no MACD overlay.

TRADING FUNDAMENTALS
What is Limit Order vs Market Order?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

Market orders seek prompt execution at available prices. Limit orders set a price boundary and may remain unfilled. Choosing an order type involves a trade-off between execution priority and price control.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A market order requests execution at available prices without setting a maximum buy or minimum sell price. A limit order sets that boundary, but may fill partly or not at all. A last-traded price is not a commitment that the same quantity is available now. For a hypothetical example, suppose the ask shows $20 for only five shares while a buyer wants ten. A market fill may reach higher offers. A $20 buy limit cannot execute above $20, but the unfilled quantity may remain open or expire according to its instructions. A stop-market instruction, by contrast, becomes a market order after its trigger and does not promise the trigger price. Compare prices, completion, delays and modeled costs separately rather than assume an order type ensures better financial results. TradeHQ supports simplified virtual market orders only; it does not operate an exchange order book or pending orders.

KEY POINTS
Market orders request execution at available prices; fills and price depend on liquidity
Limit orders: a price boundary, not an exact fill price; they may remain unfilled
Limit prices constrain execution price, without ensuring a fill or preventing loss
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare price control with execution uncertainty. A market order prioritises execution at available prices; a limit order sets a price boundary but may not fill. TradeHQ currently executes market practice orders only.

Worked exercise and its limits

Suppose a quoted ask is $10 but the next available fill is $10.20. A market purchase may fill at $10.20; a $10 buy limit cannot fill above its limit and may remain unfilled. TradeHQ supports market orders only.

What is Stop Loss Hunting?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A suspected intentional move through levels where stop orders may be placed. A price reversal alone does not prove manipulation, identify a trader or reveal actual order locations.

DETAILED DEFINITION

Stop loss hunting is a term used for a suspected intentional move through levels where stop orders may be placed. A chart showing a move through such a level does not establish manipulation, the identity of a trader or actual order locations. Distinguish a suspected explanation from observable prices, actual order records and findings by a market authority; similar chart movements can have different causes. In a hypothetical example, several participants could choose exits below a recent low. If the market trades through those levels, triggered sell orders could add to selling pressure. That example describes a possible order-flow mechanism, rather than evidence that actual orders were concentrated there or that another participant deliberately moved the price. A later reversal could reflect new orders, changing liquidity, news or other causes. A wick records an interval's price range; it is not a visual signature proving a completed hunt. Public order books show displayed orders, while stop instructions, hidden orders and positions may not be publicly visible. Liquidation estimates and third-party heatmaps also require a clearly identified data source and methodology; they do not reveal every account or the location of the next price move. Charts aggregate trades over a chosen interval, so changing the interval can change how an apparent sweep looks. To examine a suspected event, first record the instrument, venue, observation time, price and volume data. Separate that record from assumptions about hidden orders or participant intent. Compare other plausible explanations and avoid treating a single chart pattern as proof. Trading safeguards involve trade-offs. A stop-market instruction can execute at a different price from its trigger, a stop-limit instruction can remain unfilled, and an unsubmitted mental exit is not an exchange order. Changing a stop level or using a time-based exit cannot guarantee protection against loss or an adverse move. TradeHQ's simulator currently supports market practice orders rather than automated stops. Its displayed practice charts should not be treated as forensic evidence about actual exchange manipulation.

KEY POINTS
Describes a suspected mechanism, rather than proving actual stop locations
A reversal after a level breaks does not establish deliberate manipulation
No stop buffer or exit method guarantees protection against loss
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

A stop can be triggered before price reverses for many ordinary reasons, including volatility, clustered order flow, spread changes, and the level you chose. Avoid assuming manipulation without evidence; review the market structure and your placement instead.

Worked exercise and its limits

An invented move from $100 to $98 and back to $101 may cross an assumed stop at $99. Compare an ordinary liquidity change and alleged manipulation as competing explanations. The price path alone cannot decide between them; no resting stop order is supported here.

TRADING FUNDAMENTALS
What is Leverage Trading?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

Leverage is exposure greater than the supporting equity or collateral; losses can exceed the initial investment. At 10x leverage, $1,000 of margin controls roughly $10,000 of exposure. Leverage amplifies both gains and losses.

DETAILED DEFINITION

Leverage describes notional exposure relative to the equity or collateral supporting it. A hypothetical $1,000 margin amount supporting $10,000 exposure gives a 10-to-one ratio. A 10% adverse price move on that exposure is $1,000 before costs, but this is not a liquidation formula. Initial and maintenance requirements, eligible collateral, other positions, fees and venue rules all matter. A loan-funded share purchase differs from a futures performance bond or a perpetual contract. Product eligibility and maximum permitted exposure vary by jurisdiction, customer category, broker and instrument. An advertised maximum is neither permission for a particular user nor a recommendation. TradeHQ’s ordinary spot practice orders do not borrow money or reproduce a leveraged account. A worksheet can compare price shocks, account equity and cash-flow demands while keeping legal eligibility and actual margin terms as separate questions. Hypothetical worksheet: an account with $1,500 equity and $10,000 exposure loses $300 on a 3% adverse move before fees. Equity becomes $1,200. The initial exposure-to-account-equity ratio was about 6.67, even if only $1,000 had been labelled posted margin. This is why the denominator and eligible collateral must be stated; no exchange liquidation threshold is supplied by that arithmetic.

References
CME — futures margin mechanics (distinct from a stock loan)
KEY POINTS
Greater exposure relative to equity magnifies linear gains and losses before costs; actual product outcomes can differ
Liquidation depends on maintenance requirements and venue rules and can occur before the deposit is exhausted
No universal professional leverage limit is established here
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Use a hypothetical exposure-to-equity calculation to compare gains and losses. TradeHQ does not implement leverage, and completing the exercise does not establish suitability for a real margin account.

Worked exercise and its limits

Compare unleveraged $1,000 exposure with $10,000 exposure supported by $1,000 collateral. A 2% adverse move means $20 versus $200 before costs. This linear illustration omits liquidation and funding; the TradeHQ order engine is unleveraged.

What is FOMO (Fear of Missing Out)?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

FOMO is the anxiety-driven urge to trade because a price is moving or others appear to be profiting. The emotion does not identify a market top or establish a measured win rate.

DETAILED DEFINITION

FOMO means fear of missing out. In market discussions it can describe concern about missing apparent gains or pressure to imitate a publicly shared trade. The label does not diagnose a condition, identify someone’s motives from their purchase or measure future returns. Selectively published gains omit unknown losses, costs and unsuccessful participants. A learner can record what was known before a simulated decision and what was learned later, keeping the price outcome separate from the quality of the reasoning. No neurological claim, universal loss rate or promise that journaling improves returns is established here.

KEY POINTS
Emotional response to seeing rapid price increases
Emotion alone does not establish where a market top is or a measured loss probability
A written record separates the available information from later outcomes; it does not establish emotional or investment benefits
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare the recorded reason for a virtual decision with the information available at that time. The exercise does not diagnose a person or distinguish professionals from amateurs.

Worked exercise and its limits

Write down what information was available before an imagined purchase and what was learned later. Separate a rising price from a claim that everyone else profited. This record cannot diagnose a person or establish the effect of an emotion on future prices.

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

FUD means fear, uncertainty and doubt. The label is often applied to negative claims; it does not establish whether a claim is true, false or deliberately manipulative.

FUD means fear, uncertainty and doubt. It is often applied to negative claims about a company, token or market. Calling a claim FUD does not establish whether it is accurate, mistaken or intentionally deceptive. Identify the original source, publication date, evidence and exact allegation; distinguish a regulatory announcement from commentary about its likely price effects. A later price rise does not disprove an earlier risk, and a decline does not verify every allegation. The exercise concerns information checking rather than diagnosing emotions, inferring a short seller’s motives or forecasting a market response.

Can be legitimate concerns or deliberate manipulation
Negative claims can spread on social media; check their source and evidence
Always verify FUD claims through official sources before reacting
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Check a negative claim’s original source and date. A concern can be material, mistaken or uncertain; a prior thesis does not turn every adverse report into a buying opportunity.

Take a fictional alarming headline and separate its factual claim, original source, publication date and interpretation. Explain why labelling it FUD neither disproves the claim nor establishes the author's motive.

What is HODL Strategy?

HODL is a buy-and-hold expression associated with a Bitcoin forum typo. Holding through volatility can still produce losses; neither a four-year period nor an earlier price history guarantees recovery.

DETAILED DEFINITION

HODL is informal language for retaining a crypto holding through price fluctuations. It is not a contractual protection, a guaranteed recovery rule or a distinct instrument. A single purchase and a recurring contribution schedule are different cash flows, and either can be held for a long period. A token can lose most or all of its value, become difficult to sell or be lost through custody failure. A published issuance rule alone cannot establish demand, purchasing power or future price. The linked Bitcoin white paper explains the protocol proposal; it does not validate a profitable holding strategy.

KEY POINTS
Originated from a 2013 Bitcoin forum typo ('HODL' instead of 'HOLD')
Fewer transactions may reduce trading costs while price and timing risks remain
A holding period does not protect against permanent loss, custody failure or illiquidity
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare a hypothetical holding period with an exit case, including permanent loss. Holding longer does not remove emotional decisions or guarantee a recovery.

Worked exercise and its limits

For an invented $1,000 holding, compare end values of $1,400, $600 and zero after the same period. Holding without selling does not remove market loss or custody risk. The white paper is protocol background, not evidence for a profitable holding strategy.

What is Satoshi Nakamoto?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

Satoshi Nakamoto is the pseudonym used by the creator of Bitcoin, who published its whitepaper in 2008. Identity and ownership of wallets attributed to the creator remain uncertain.

DETAILED DEFINITION

Satoshi Nakamoto is the name attached to the Bitcoin white paper, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System. The document proposes electronic payments using cryptographic proof and a distributed timestamp mechanism. The name does not establish a verified individual identity. Claims about personal wealth, motives or ownership of particular early-mined coins require evidence beyond the paper and are not established here. Reading the original proposal helps separate its protocol design from later commentary about Bitcoin’s investment value. Neither the author’s identity nor a protocol description supplies a forecast of token prices.

KEY POINTS
Published the Bitcoin whitepaper on October 31, 2008
Wallet attribution and estimated holdings are uncertain; no exact ownership total is asserted here
True identity remains unknown — one of tech's biggest mysteries
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Bitcoin's 2008 proposal drew on earlier cryptographic research. Reading the dated announcement and its references helps distinguish the documented protocol from later claims about the author's identity and holdings.

Worked exercise and its limits

Read the white paper's title, author name and timestamp proposal. Separate statements in the document from later claims about the author's identity or holdings. A pseudonym and address analysis do not establish a verified real-world identity.

What is Margin Call?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A demand for additional collateral under an account’s margin terms. A broker may reduce or liquidate positions under its rules; a call does not guarantee a response period.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A margin call concerns collateral under a particular account agreement. In a loan-funded securities account, equity is the marked asset value less the loan and relevant obligations. Initial and maintenance requirements differ, and a broker can impose house requirements or change them. Futures performance-bond arrangements are a different mechanism from borrowing to purchase shares. Do not transfer a percentage or deadline between products. The linked SEC bulletin warns that a brokerage may sell securities without consulting the customer and that an extension is not an entitlement. Depositing collateral, reducing exposure or liquidation can change the account, but none guarantees a chosen exit price or caps every loss. TradeHQ has no margin accounts. Use the hypothetical equity calculation below to study the denominator, then keep actual broker procedures as a separate source-reading question.

KEY POINTS
Collateral obligations depend on the account agreement and maintenance rules; forced closing can occur without a prior call
A broker may reduce or liquidate positions under its agreement; no guaranteed warning or response window is implied
Multiple simultaneous margin calls can amplify market crashes
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Read the relevant maintenance and liquidation terms. A margin call can require action quickly, and no lesson or alert guarantees time to respond. TradeHQ has no margin accounts.

Worked exercise and its limits

Hypothetical account: $10,000 securities minus a $6,000 loan leave $4,000 equity. If securities fall to $8,000 with the loan unchanged, equity is $2,000, or 25% of asset value. Compare a stated maintenance requirement; do not invent the broker's call or liquidation procedure.

What is Liquidation Price?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

A liquidation price is an estimate of the level at which a leveraged position may be closed under a platform's margin rules. Collateral, fees, other positions and the pricing method can change that estimate.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A liquidation price is a venue-calculated threshold used in managing a collateralized position. It is not necessarily an executable price or the price that consumes every dollar of equity. Maintenance requirements, other positions, eligible collateral, fees, funding and mark-price rules affect the threshold. Actual closing orders may execute differently during a gap or liquidity shortage. Isolated and cross-margin arrangements allocate eligible collateral differently; neither label establishes a universal cap on losses or account obligations. Consult a specific contract and venue rules for an actual calculation. TradeHQ’s unleveraged spot simulation has no liquidation-price engine.

KEY POINTS
With other inputs fixed, greater exposure leaves less collateral buffer; an exact threshold depends on the applicable rules
Isolated-margin treatment depends on the platform rules; it is not a universal loss guarantee
Mark price vs last price affects when liquidation triggers
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare the inputs in a venue’s documented estimate rather than treating one displayed price as fixed. Margin requirements and other positions can change the result.

Worked exercise and its limits

Distinguish a simplified collateral-loss calculation from an actual venue liquidation price. Fees, maintenance tiers, mark prices and collateral mode affect the latter. No single entry-price/leverage formula establishes a universal guaranteed exit, and TradeHQ does not model liquidation.
